feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (no completions, all 60 trials off-track, max_error 0.062 to 0.069, line loss 1 to 2, oscillation 0.07 to 0.15) showed that the array's span was the first limit. Iteration 1 (±0.03 m, 16 mm, kp 3.0, kd 0.1) barely moved the score (49.47 to 50.13): line loss stayed at 1 per track and max_error stayed at 0.0615 to 0.0687, so the span is not the main limit. I built this package on the Builder's y = 0.04 m lead and kept the iteration 1 controller so the lead change is isolated. Interpret the next race as follows. If line_loss_events reaches 0 on the slalom and s-bend and max_error stays below 0.06, keep the 0.04 m lead and move to speed (mass or wheel radius). If line loss or max_error ≥ 0.06 persists on the slalom or s-bend, the sensors are not reaching far enough to catch the tape at the bends, so widen the span further. If the robot finishes the course slowly, or holds the line and still exceeds 3.0 s, the limit is speed.
requested_changes: If the next race still shows line_loss_events ≥ 1 or max_error ≥ 0.06 on the slalom or s-bend (iteration 1 showed this at y = 0.05 m), widen the span to x = ±0.04 m (x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04) with sensor_size 0.016 and keep weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]; iteration 1 shows ±0.03 m alone did not stop line loss.

If the next race keeps the line (line_loss_events 0, max_error < 0.06) but completion_time stays above 3.0 s, reduce mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg or raise wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.035 m; iteration 1 progress of 0.10 to 0.15 with no completions suggests the robot is leaving the track before the speed limit matters, so change speed only after line loss is fixed.

If the next race shows max_error rising above the iteration 1 value (0.0615 to 0.0687) after the lead change, return the sensors to y = 0.05 m and try sensor_size 0.012 at ±0.03 m; iteration 0 (12 mm footprint) and iteration 1 (16 mm footprint) differed in both span and footprint, so the footprint effect is not yet isolated.
